sections.what: CommunityHealth provides medical, dental, medication and mental health care at Chicago sites. Its giving page identifies EIN 36-3831793. Dental waiting lists indicate unmet demand but do not establish whether money or volunteers constrain supply.
sections.monitoring: The 2024 report counts 4,147 patients, 24,695 visits and 23,579 prescriptions. Only patients enter the model, preventing duplicate credit across services. Request baseline illness, deduplicated clinical response, sustained utility, alternative care and resident county. The Oregon randomized Medicaid study increased utilization and reduced depression but found no significant measured physical-health gains in two years; coverage is not a direct trial of this clinic, and supplies no numerical calibration here.
sections.qualitative: Medical access can improve pain, function and mental health. Donated clinicians and medicines may stretch cash but their availability can constrain expansion. Financial relief and education have nonhealth value outside this QALY estimate. Mortality and all other net health are provisionally zero, not a proven lower bound.
sections.cost: Full 2024 audited expense is $21,453,697, including $12,728,899 consumed donated inventory, $3,995,847 donated services and $177,307 other in-kind expenses. Use expense rather than $12,475,722 inventory received. Model: 4,147 patients × 0.30 additional clinically improved share × 0.05 utility × 0.5 year × 0.4 funding additionality × 0.98 MSA share. This is an illustrative scenario, not a measured expected value or marginal purchase price.
sections.funding: Audit issued November 13, 2025 reports revenue $21,052,293, net assets $6,621,698 and donor restrictions $684,948. Government grants $1,000,893 and volunteer constraints make gift additionality uncertain. Full recipient overhead remains. In-kind expense totals $16,902,053; excluding it gives $4,551,644 cash-like expense, not cash flow, shown only as a sensitivity. No priced unfunded expansion was found.

model.costScope: Full audited recipient costs including recognized donated resources; external hospital resources not included. Recognized pharmaceutical wholesale values and donated-provider billing rates are accounting amounts, not measured opportunity costs.
model.counterfactual: a removes equivalent care elsewhere and ineffective care; b separately removes replacement financing/volunteer capacity. One morbidity pathway avoids double counting.
model.geographicAttribution: Current service sites are in Cook County. g=.98 is judged resident share, not observed; pinned 13-county MSA excludes Kenosha.
model.uncertainty: Central illustrative scenario and favorable/poor bounds are judgments, not calibrated EV or confidence interval. Cross-recipient results cannot be summed without deduplication. These costs are whole-portfolio equivalents, not marginal gift purchase guarantees. Cost numerators use different accounting recognition of donated care; central prices must not be interpreted as a comparable economic-efficiency ranking. Favorable and poor scenarios are illustrative cases, not exhaustive bounds.
